{#f4q4} Patients who had postoperative complications (Clavien–Dindo classification ≥ II) underwent more frequent lobectomy (82.9% versus 75.7%, p = 0.023), pneumonectomy (5.7% versus 0.6%, p = 0.023). Conversion to open thoracotomy was also more common (10.2% versus 1.3%, p = 0.007) along with longer surgical time (130 min [SD: 42.6] versus 112.5 min, [SD: 37.2], p = 0.002). These patients exhibited higher rate of postoperative pulmonary complications (p < 0.001), and longer hospital stay (10 days [IQR: 7.2, 14.8] versus 7 days [IQR 6, 8], p < 0.001) (Table 3). Open thoracotomy was associated with increased incidence of postoperative pulmonary complications (91.2% versus 77.6%, p = 0.012) and longer hospital stays (8 days [IQR: 6, 11] versus 6 days [IQR: 5, 7], p < 0.001) compared to VATS procedures (Table 4).

{#yh0t} # Discussion

{#b9g3} Our study investigated the outcomes of lung cancer surgery in elderly patients, focusing on postoperative complications and mortality rates. We observed an in-hospital mortality rate of 1.7% after lung cancer surgery. Benker et al. [@w:w6] reported an overall operative mortality rate of 1.56%, similar to our finding. In contrast, Detillon et al. [@w:w7] found a higher operative mortality rate by 2.1% in patients ≥ 60 years with lung cancer resections compared to our data.

{#djza} ## Postoperative complications

{#vkpz} We found that 28.9% of patients experienced postoperative pulmonary complications and 12.6% experienced cardiac complications classified as Clavien–Dindo grade ≥ II. These rates are higher compared to the previous studies reporting 10–15.4% for pulmonary complications in elderly patients undergoing lung resection [@w:w8]. Similary, Calado et al. [@w:w9] reported lower cardiac complications rates (8.2%) compared to our findings. In contrast, Srisomboon et al. [@w:w10] reported higher rate of respiratory (25%) and lower rates of cardiac complications (6%) in elderly patients undergoing thoracoscopic surgery.

Performing VATS, when possible, could reduce the incidence of postoperative complications, especially pulmonary complications, in elderly patients. However, we found that conversion from VATS to open thoracotomy significantly increased the incidence of postoperative complications. This may be caused by surgical complications or bleeding that leads to increased surgical time, blood loss, and transfusion of blood products, which then leads to increased postoperative complications.

{#d7ux} # Introduction

{#ex2n} Lung cancer is the most frequently occurring cancer and the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide . Pulmonary resection is key treatment for lung cancer but is often accompanied by significant postoperative complications, which may prolong hospital stay and incur greater medical expenses [@w:w1]. Surgical approaches for lung cancer, including video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and thoracotomy, offer distinct advantages and challenges. Previous studies [@w:w2] suggest that VATS is superior to thoracotomy due to fewer postoperative complications.

{#fb1h} Patients undergoing thoracic surgery were more likely to be older. Poor physiological changes are common in elderly patients with complex comorbidities, which could complicate major noncardiac surgery, especially thoracic surgery, and negatively impact outcomes [@w:w3]. It is imperative to evaluate better risk indicators to improve preoperative cardiac risk prediction in elderly patients.
